How Jefferson County, Washington, Conducts Tax Sales – A Step-by-Step Guide

Jefferson County, Washington, holds tax sales to recover unpaid property taxes. When property owners fail to pay taxes, the county auctions off the property to collect what is owed. These tax sales happen online, allowing investors to bid from anywhere. If you’re thinking about joining a tax auction, here’s everything you need to know.

How the Auction Works

Jefferson County conducts tax sales through an online auction platform. Here’s how to participate:

  1. Register on the auction website before placing bids.
  2. Pay a $550 deposit to qualify for bidding.
  3. $50 of the deposit is non-refundable, covering auction platform fees.
  4. If you don’t win, you get a $500 refund after the auction.
  5. If you win but don’t pay, you forfeit your deposit, and the property goes back up for auction.
  6. The starting bid covers delinquent taxes, interest, penalties, and fees.
  7. A 5% buyer’s premium is added to the final price.

Preparing for the Auction

Tax sales offer great investment opportunities, but they come with risks. Jefferson County sells all properties as-is and does not guarantee their condition or legal status. Research is essential before placing any bids.

Jefferson County tax sales happen regularly, and new properties are added all the time. Since auction details can change, staying informed is essential.

Check the auction calendar often so you don’t miss opportunities.

Key Steps to Take Before Bidding

  1. Review the property list – Check the county’s foreclosure list and verify property details.
  2. Investigate title issues – Look for existing liens, easements, or legal disputes.
  3. Confirm location and boundaries – Use county records or maps to verify property lines.
  4. Understand permitted uses – Research zoning laws to know what you can do with the property.
  5. Check for occupancy – Some properties may still have tenants or previous owners.

Some properties may have legal claims or unpaid obligations. Contact the county treasurer’s office and check public records to avoid costly surprises.

Payment and Deadlines

Winning bidders must pay the full purchase price within the county’s deadline. Jefferson County only accepts electronic funds transfers (EFT).

What You Need to Know About Payments

  • Full payment must be made on time – No extensions or late payments.
  • Only EFT payments are accepted – No cash, checks, or credit cards.
  • Confirm payment receipt – Ensure the county has received your payment before the deadline.

If you fail to pay on time, the county keeps your deposit and relists the property for auction.

Receiving the Deed

After the county receives full payment, it issues a tax deed to the winning bidder. This process can take up to 30 days.

Important Things to Know About the Deed

  1. The deed transfers ownership but does not guarantee a clear title.
  2. Outstanding liens may still exist, meaning you could owe additional money.
  3. Legal disputes are possible, especially from previous owners or creditors.
  4. Encumbrances, such as easements, may affect how you use the property.

To protect your investment, consider title insurance or consult a real estate attorney before making further plans.

What Happens After You Win

Once you receive the deed, you become responsible for the property immediately.

Your Next Steps as the New Owner

  • Handle occupants – If tenants or previous owners are still living on the property, you must follow legal eviction procedures.
  • Resolve title issues – If liens or claims exist, it’s your responsibility to clear them.
  • Develop, rent, or sell – Depending on your investment goals, you can improve, lease, or resell the property.
